brief:
GS's Q3 earnings preview expects S&P 500 EPS growth of 27% year over year, down from 33% in Q2. AI infrastructure beneficiaries drive over half of that growth as hyperscaler capex grows 116%, while the median stock's growth slows from 14% to 9% on cost pressure and a smaller dollar tailwind. GS expects another quarter of beats, helped by fading private equity distortions and tariff refunds, about 6% of pre tax profits each quarter.

In semis, after a two month pullback (SOX down 11% vs SPX up 4%) GS turns more constructive into 3Q: positive SemiCap revisions, upside for server CPUs and ASICs, and preference for HDDs and NAND within memory.

In banks, capital markets normalize but stay up year over year, NII benefits from loan growth offset by deposit costs, and capital deployment moderates on G-SIB buffers. GS favors WFC (Conviction List), BAC and C.

On Boeing, union ratification and F/A-XX win are positive and the FAA cleared the 737 MAX software issue, so GS stays Buy rated.

The market update flags balanced HF and asset manager flows, rising Semis demand on MU earnings and NVDA's buyback increase, and the S&P down a seventh straight week on Tech concentration.
